title: Em-dash ban violated in 5 new implementer-authored success toasts (and the attempt-log export joins)
location: client/src/copy.gleam:874-884 (refcheck_toast_started / refcheck_toast_re_enabled / refcheck_toast_taken_over / refcheck_toast_corrected / refcheck_toast_substituted); client/src/client.gleam:6777-6784 (build_attempt_log_text)
evidence:
pub const refcheck_toast_started: String = "Reference started — the invite goes out now."
pub const refcheck_toast_re_enabled: String = "Reference re-enabled — it's back in the queue."
pub const refcheck_toast_taken_over: String = "You're handling this one — automated messages stopped."
pub const refcheck_toast_corrected: String = "Details saved — the invitation is on its way again."
pub const refcheck_toast_substituted: String = "Referee substituted — the new invitation is on its way."
--- build_attempt_log_text (client/src/client.gleam) ---
attempt.at <> " — " <> attempt.channel <> " — " <> attempt.outcome
--- pin gap (client/test/copy_test.gleam:296-315) ---
for_each_copy only scans copy.toast(code, ctx) / copy.page(code, ctx); no_em_dash_test therefore never sees the refcheck_* constants
detail: Round guard 9 / RC4.2 r2 carried warning: the repo-wide em-dash ban (no_em_dash_test panics on any landlord-facing string) does not scan refcheck copy — new implementer-authored strings must be checked by hand. The UX spec fixes no verbatim copy for these five success toasts (the only spec-fixed toast, §7.6 'Attempt log copied — paste it into your records or a message.', is itself deferred to RC4.4 by the PR's own comment), so they are implementer-authored and the ban applies: all five contain U+2014. The attempt-log export additionally composes its lines with ' — ' joins — the same em-dash composition-site pattern the carried warning calls out for the timeline. The strings render in the landlord SPA (toast channel) and the exported log lands in landlord records/messages.
recommended_fix: Replace the em-dashes with a period or comma (e.g. 'Reference started. The invite goes out now.', 'You're handling this one — automated messages stopped.' -> 'You're handling this one. Automated messages stopped.'), and use a non-em-dash separator (e.g. ' | ') in build_attempt_log_text.

title: Stale refcheck-action response is NOT dropped by the claimed id-match guard — can wipe another application's in-progress edit form
location: client/src/client.gleam:3512-3552 (ApiReturnedRefcheckAction handler); comments at client/src/client.gleam:6583-6585 and client/src/msg.gleam:274-275
detail: The handler contains no route check, no call_id-vs-current-detail check, and no match against the confirm/edit surface — the 'id-match guard' the comments promise does not exist. Only the fire paths are guarded (fire_refcheck_slot_action no-ops when the call is absent from the current detail). A slow action fired on application A that resolves after the landlord navigates to application B unconditionally clears B's refcheck_edit/refcheck_confirm (typed correction/substitute input is lost), shows a success/error toast for A's action in B's context, and triggers a refetch of whichever detail is current. No cross-user exposure or authz impact (all state is the landlord's own), but the false documentation and cross-application state bleed are a real defect: the same id-mismatch guard pattern used by ApiReturnedReportPdf (report_download_loading match) was not applied here.
recommended_fix: Carry the vacancy/application ids on ApiReturnedRefcheckAction and no-op the handler unless the route still matches those ids (mirroring the ApiReturnedReportPdf id-mismatch guard), or at minimum require call_id to be present in the current application_detail before clearing/toasting.
